$comment: Conformance cases for a recorded-history store (src/data/historyRecords.js). Language-neutral: any store, in any language, should pass every case.

Fields named t, receivedAt, fromMs, toMs and now given as strings are ISO 8601 times ("NaN" stands for NaN) and become epoch milliseconds. null is an absent optional number. {"$repeat": s, "times": n} is s repeated n times.

Steps: write (expect: counts, rejected by index, coverage counts), query (read every page with pageSize, default 1000, and compare the concatenation), coverage, queryError (expect a code), cursorReuse (take the first page's cursor and pass it to another query; code 'none' means it must be accepted), prune (expect droppedDays). A case's open options go to the store.

cases.name: round-trip
cases.clause: Every field of an accepted record reads back unchanged; absent optional numbers read back absent; negative zero, in any field, reads back as zero.

cases.name: time-kind
cases.clause: The clock a time was read from is kept with it.

cases.name: provenance
cases.clause: A query returns observed records unless it names other provenances, so derived and simulated positions never pass as observed.

cases.name: repeat-and-conflict
cases.clause: A record identical to a stored one is a repeat; a different record for a stored source, key and time is a conflict and the stored record stays.

cases.name: sources-isolated
cases.clause: The same key and time in two sources are two records; a query sees one source.

cases.name: midnight
cases.clause: A track that crosses UTC midnight reads back in time order across the boundary, a page at a time; a time exactly at midnight belongs to the new day; both query bounds are inclusive.

cases.name: utf8-key-order
cases.clause: Records at one time are ordered by key in UTF-8 byte order, which puts U+FF5E before U+1F600 (UTF-16 order would not).

cases.name: paging-ties
cases.clause: Paging through records that share a time, across a day boundary, returns each record exactly once whatever the page size.

cases.name: cursor-binding
cases.clause: A cursor continues only the query that issued it (same source, range, provenance and keys; the page size may change); another query, or text that is not a cursor, is refused.

cases.name: keys-filter
cases.clause: A query naming keys returns only those keys, in the usual order.

cases.name: validation
cases.clause: A malformed record is refused by index with the field that is wrong, and the rest of the batch is written. Keys of 256 UTF-8 bytes are accepted, 258 refused; a key with a lone surrogate (no UTF-8 form) and a fractional millisecond are refused.

cases.name: query-errors
cases.clause: A query with a reversed or fractional range, bad limit, empty provenance or key list, a key or source with no UTF-8 form, or no source is refused with a stable code.

cases.name: flags
cases.clause: BREAK and FLOOR are kept; LIVE, time-kind bits and unknown bits are not stored.

cases.name: coverage
cases.clause: Coverage intervals that touch merge; a recorder outage stays a hole; an interval across midnight reads back whole; the answer is clipped to the query; bad intervals are refused.

cases.name: retention
cases.clause: Pruning with a retention of N days drops whole UTC days older than the newest N, today included, with their records and coverage.
